questions.stem: CLZ-340 stores a generated password in Key Vault. Which storage still requires secret protection?

options.A: Only the public README
options.B: Only the vault's DNS name

optionExplanations.A: The README contains no generated password.
optionExplanations.B: The name is metadata, not the value.
optionExplanations.C: The Terraform resources record secret values in state.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not contain the generated value.

questions.stem: A sensitive value is hidden in ordinary terraform output. What does that establish?

options.A: Display redaction, not removal from Terraform state
options.B: Encryption of every local state file

optionExplanations.A: Sensitive markings suppress normal display.
optionExplanations.B: State encryption needs separate protection.
optionExplanations.C: Marking a value does not rotate it.
optionExplanations.D: Saved plans may contain sensitive data.

questions.stem: Which CLI query follows the lesson's secret validation approach?

options.A: Print secret value into a transcript
options.B: Query secret id and attributes.enabled
options.D: Export every secret as a public artifact

optionExplanations.A: That leaks secret material to logs.
optionExplanations.B: It validates metadata without displaying the credential.
optionExplanations.C: The generated secret must not be published.
optionExplanations.D: Public artifacts are an inappropriate secret store.

questions.stem: Which value matches key_vault_access_cidr's intended workstation restriction?

options.A: Entire Internet 0.0.0.0/0
options.B: Private laptop address 192.168.1.5/32

optionExplanations.A: The input deliberately rejects broad exposure.
optionExplanations.B: An Internet request arrives from public egress, not private LAN IP.
optionExplanations.C: This lab variable is IPv4-specific.
optionExplanations.D: The lesson admits one current public IPv4.

questions.stem: Secret access worked yesterday but returns Forbidden after changing networks. What should be checked?

options.A: Whether the vault tag count increased
options.B: Whether the secret name has a hyphen
options.C: Whether Terraform files were sorted alphabetically
options.D: Current public egress IP against the allowed /32

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not admit data-plane traffic.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson secret name is valid.
optionExplanations.C: File ordering does not control network admission.
optionExplanations.D: The firewall still may admit only the old public IP.

questions.stem: A client IP is allowed but secret access fails. What independent control must be verified?

options.A: Only the public DNS TTL
options.B: The signed-in identity's secret permissions

optionExplanations.A: DNS caching is not a secret access policy.
optionExplanations.B: Network admission does not grant secret authorization.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson has no storage replication setting.
optionExplanations.D: This lesson deploys no VM.

questions.stem: az keyvault show succeeds while secret access is denied by the firewall. Why is that possible?

options.A: Vault management and secret data operations have different access paths
options.B: A management read automatically grants every secret permission

optionExplanations.A: Management visibility does not prove data-plane reachability or authorization.
optionExplanations.B: Management permissions do not grant all data operations.
optionExplanations.C: A denial does not mean the secret is absent.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform's secret resource still needs permitted access.

questions.stem: Which principal receives the access policy in CLZ-340?

options.A: Every Internet user
options.B: Only Azure Bastion's IP address
options.C: The applying identity returned by azurerm_client_config

optionExplanations.A: The policy is not anonymous.
optionExplanations.B: An IP is not the identity object ID.
optionExplanations.C: The data source supplies the active tenant and object IDs.
optionExplanations.D: The policy is not tenant-wide subscription delegation.

questions.stem: Which production change reduces broad routine secret-administration permissions?

options.A: Give all consumers Purge and Set
options.B: Use Azure RBAC and separate administrators from secret consumers
options.D: Store the secret in a public Git tag

optionExplanations.A: Consumers generally do not need destructive administration.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson recommends role separation and RBAC.
optionExplanations.C: Network controls do not replace authentication.
optionExplanations.D: Git tags are public metadata, not secret stores.

questions.stem: A no-change plan should preserve the vault's suffix. Which practice supports that?

options.A: Regenerate the suffix on every login
options.B: Rename the vault directly in the portal
options.C: Use a timestamp as every plan's suffix

optionExplanations.A: Logins should not rotate resource naming.
optionExplanations.B: Manual changes do not preserve declared ownership.
optionExplanations.C: Per-run timestamps cause name churn.
optionExplanations.D: The generated value persists in Terraform state.

questions.stem: A deleted vault name is unavailable for immediate reuse. What should be investigated?

options.A: Only the secret's enabled flag
options.B: Only the NSG priority
options.C: Soft-deleted vault retention and organization policy

optionExplanations.A: Secret enabled status does not free a vault name.
optionExplanations.B: No NSG is deployed here.
optionExplanations.C: Retained soft-deleted vaults reserve their names.
optionExplanations.D: No Windows VM is deployed here.

questions.stem: What does soft delete provide after accidental secret deletion?

options.A: A recovery window before final deletion
options.B: An anonymous read endpoint

optionExplanations.A: Recoverability is bounded by the configured retention policy.
optionExplanations.B: Deletion does not grant anonymous access.
optionExplanations.C: Retention is finite.
optionExplanations.D: No tenant migration is implied.

questions.stem: Why should a production vault enable purge protection despite the disposable-lab exception?

options.A: To prevent permanent purge during the protected retention interval
options.B: To reveal passwords in CLI output

optionExplanations.A: It protects the recovery interval from early permanent deletion.
optionExplanations.B: Output disclosure is unrelated.
optionExplanations.C: Authorization is still required.
optionExplanations.D: Protection is not a zero-cost pricing tier.

questions.stem: Why is routine Purge permission called out as a production gap in this lesson?

options.A: It makes secret creation impossible
options.B: It disables the storage firewall
options.C: It can permanently remove recoverable secret material when protection permits

optionExplanations.A: Purge is not a ban on creation.
optionExplanations.B: Storage rules are unrelated.
optionExplanations.C: Purge is a destructive capability that needs separation.
optionExplanations.D: The permission is more powerful than metadata reads.

questions.stem: The firewall uses bypass=AzureServices. What should a learner avoid assuming?

options.A: That the supplied /32 is an IPv4 rule
options.B: That default_action=Deny restricts ordinary public clients
options.D: That every Azure-hosted application automatically bypasses the firewall

optionExplanations.A: The /32 really is an IPv4 boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Default deny is a relevant access restriction.
optionExplanations.C: Authorization remains necessary.
optionExplanations.D: The trusted-services exception is limited, not blanket Azure access.

questions.stem: A disposable rotation changes the generated password. What must be reviewed before applying?

options.A: Only the random suffix's text color
options.B: Consumers and secret-bearing state or plan implications

optionExplanations.A: Presentation color does not assess rotation.
optionExplanations.B: Credential rotation affects consumers and sensitive artifacts.
optionExplanations.C: Line count does not describe consumers.
optionExplanations.D: A valid region is not enough to assess secret impact.

questions.stem: Which use is demonstrated by the windows-admin-password secret?

options.A: Automatic IIS installation
options.B: Terraform backend locking
options.C: Central storage of a generated credential

optionExplanations.A: IIS deployment is a different lesson.
optionExplanations.B: Backend locking uses state storage.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson stores a secret; it does not deploy its consumer.
optionExplanations.D: No autoscale resource is created here.

questions.stem: After CLZ-340 apply, which resource should not be claimed as deployed by this lesson?

options.A: A Standard Key Vault
options.B: A Windows VM consuming the secret

optionExplanations.A: The vault is explicitly configured.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson generates a credential without deploying a VM.
optionExplanations.C: The secret resource is explicitly configured.
optionExplanations.D: The random naming resource is explicitly configured.

questions.stem: Why use the configured random_password resource instead of a shared sample password?

options.A: It creates a strong per-deployment value with defined character requirements
options.B: It removes the password from state

optionExplanations.A: Generation avoids reusing a known sample credential.
optionExplanations.B: The generated result is still stored in state.
optionExplanations.C: No database role is managed here.
optionExplanations.D: Handling and logging can still disclose it.

questions.stem: A saved plan contains the generated secret. Where should that plan be kept?

options.A: In the public lesson download folder
options.B: In an issue attachment
options.D: In protected, untracked local storage with limited access

optionExplanations.A: Public downloads expose plan contents.
optionExplanations.B: Issue attachments can disclose sensitive data.
optionExplanations.C: Captions are public documentation.
optionExplanations.D: Plans can contain secret values and require protection.

questions.stem: A 403 tempts a learner to allow 0.0.0.0/0. What is the better first repair?

options.A: Disable all vault authorization
options.B: Verify identity, current public /32, and policy propagation
options.C: Publish the secret for easier testing

optionExplanations.A: Removing authorization weakens security.
optionExplanations.B: Diagnose the actual boundary instead of broadening exposure.
optionExplanations.C: Publication is not a connectivity repair.
optionExplanations.D: Name churn does not repair permissions.

questions.stem: Which item can materially increase cost beyond this small Standard secret lesson?

options.A: Private endpoints or high operation volume
options.B: The length of the vault's Terraform address

optionExplanations.A: Networking and service usage can change the estimate.
optionExplanations.B: Resource address length is not a billing meter.
optionExplanations.C: Documentation headings have no Azure cost.
optionExplanations.D: Prompt styling has no Azure cost.

questions.stem: Terraform destroy removes the resource group. Which caveat still applies to the vault?

options.A: All old local state backups are securely erased
options.B: Every consumer automatically gets a replacement password
options.D: Azure may retain a soft-deleted name

optionExplanations.A: Destroy does not guarantee secure erasure of every local file.
optionExplanations.B: Consumer rotation is separate.
optionExplanations.C: Soft-delete policy remains relevant.
optionExplanations.D: Service retention can survive active resource removal.

questions.stem: Which value is suitable for normal lesson evidence when no secret values are printed?

options.A: Administrator password
options.B: Raw secret-bearing state contents
options.C: Vault name and secret enabled status

optionExplanations.A: A password is sensitive credential material.
optionExplanations.B: State can contain the generated secret.
optionExplanations.C: These are metadata needed for validation.
optionExplanations.D: Plan contents may contain secrets.

questions.stem: A vault has a restricted firewall. What remains required for an admitted client's secret request?

options.A: Only a matching resource-group tag
options.B: Only a successful DNS lookup
options.C: Only knowledge of the secret name
options.D: Authentication and authorized secret operation permissions

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not authorize secret reads.
optionExplanations.B: DNS success is not permission.
optionExplanations.C: A name does not authorize a value read.
optionExplanations.D: Network access and identity authorization are distinct.

questions.stem: The lesson configures seven-day soft-delete retention. What should be considered before recreating a vault?

options.A: Retention changes automatically with every tag edit
options.B: The value controls password length
options.C: Retention is chosen at creation and retained names can affect reuse
options.D: The value defines DNS record TTL

optionExplanations.A: Tag edits do not change this interval.
optionExplanations.B: Password length is separately set to 20.
optionExplanations.C: Vault retention affects recovery and name reuse.
optionExplanations.D: DNS TTL is unrelated.

questions.stem: What evidence best completes the metadata inspection exercise?

options.A: A screenshot of the entire secret value
options.B: A sanitized result showing secret id and enabled status plus the risk explanation
options.C: The password copied to the discussion thread

optionExplanations.A: A full value screenshot leaks the credential.
optionExplanations.B: It proves the metadata check without exposing the credential.
optionExplanations.C: Discussion is not a secret store.
optionExplanations.D: State contains sensitive values.

questions.stem: An application needs to retrieve the secret without a stored application password. What production approach fits?

options.A: Managed identity with narrowly scoped secret access
options.B: Shared vault administrator credentials in source
options.C: Anonymous access through the vault firewall
options.D: Routine Purge permission for the application

optionExplanations.A: Managed identity reduces stored credentials and permits role scoping.
optionExplanations.B: Source credentials create another secret risk.
optionExplanations.C: Vault data still requires identity authorization.
optionExplanations.D: Reading a secret does not require purge administration.

questions.stem: The vault /32 was corrected after tfplan was created. Which apply preparation is safe?

options.A: Apply the existing plan because tfvars edits always replace its values
options.B: Recreate and inspect the plan with the corrected input
options.C: Edit only the printed plan summary
options.D: Assume the AzureServices bypass admits the workstation

optionExplanations.A: The saved plan is not rewritten by tfvars edits.
optionExplanations.B: Saved plans preserve planned values; regenerate after input changes.
optionExplanations.C: Displayed text is not executable plan data.
optionExplanations.D: Bypass is not a general workstation exception.

questions.stem: A secret is rotated in Key Vault but an existing consumer still uses the old password. What is missing?

options.A: A larger vault naming suffix
options.B: More secret metadata tags
options.C: A coordinated consumer update and verification

optionExplanations.A: Naming does not change consumer credentials.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not distribute passwords.
optionExplanations.C: Secret storage alone does not update every consumer.
optionExplanations.D: DNS caching does not synchronize credentials.
